Mermaid source

Preferred syntax: block. Fixed categorical cells; membership appears in comments.

Framing

The Spec Studio of the original design, docs/lineage/v0-design/07-spec-studio-and-projections.md sections 1 to 3, 11 and 12, in the order a reviewer reads it: what the Studio is and why it renders HTML; the data it reads, with the recipe answers it composes and its two named inputs, and the verb that publishes and watches it; its shell, search and navigation; its four lenses, with the index that is the Packs lens and the coverage recipe the tests lens reads; the Pack page and its maturity map; the Spec page with its core and its panels; the register pages, the owner queue, and the diff, runs and glossary pages, with the run-evidence recipe the runs page reads; the composing panel and the memo it hands off; its custom elements, the decisions that shape them, and the diagrams the engine draws for them; its phone layout; the Pack export and print; how a build is stamped and shared; and the skill that teaches an agent to publish, share and read the Studio and to apply what a person composes in it. Each Spec is followed by the examples that will verify it. Recipe 27, references into a design, shows each member's code bindings and the implemented Specs it builds on.

1. The Spec Studio is a static HTML workbench over the one graph

spec:consumers.spec-studio

The Spec Studio is a static HTML workbench over the one graph

spec:consumers.spec-studioUse Case / Behavior · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · 4 decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/spec-studio.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
actor
A person in the repository who designs a capability ahead of its code and iterates on it in passes, and a pull request reviewer who holds only a link; both read far more than they change.
problem
The generated Markdown Design Review offers no built-in search or filters, and navigation is through its links, so reviewers in the first adopter open carrier files alongside it.
outcome
Give a person reviewing a design one generated HTML workbench that explores the whole graph through lenses, shows each Spec and Pack in context, and turns a wanted change into scoped intent rather than an edit.
Behavior
rule line 27 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.sdp.md:27
The read-only Studio ships in the open-source package @libar-dev/software-delivery-protocol, beside the four shipped projections; hosted review, shared comments and hosted previews may later ship under @libar-ai/.
rule line 28 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.sdp.md:28
The Studio is a projection of the one graph: its page set under generated/spec-studio/ is regenerated from the graph, states no truth, and confers nothing back into the graph.
rule.staticPageSet line 29 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.sdp.md:29
The Studio is a static page set: the index page, which is the Packs lens; a search page; a page for each other lens, each register, the owner queue, the roadmap and the glossary; one page and one slice page per Pack, one page per Spec; one export file per Pack; and, when the build is given their inputs, a diff page and a runs page; with their local assets. Its build renders each page whole, so a page needs no server, and every page but the search page reads without its script, which adds filtering, search, copying, pan and zoom, and the composing panel.

no example exercises it

rule line 30 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.sdp.md:30
The Studio works offline: the same files open from the file system through file:// for local use and from any static host for sharing.
rule line 31 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.sdp.md:31
The Studio is reproducible: one graph and the same inputs render byte-identical files, and an asset whose filename embeds a hash of its content gets the same name from the same graph.
rule line 32 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.sdp.md:32
The Studio is read-rich: everything the graph holds about a Spec or a Pack is explorable in it.
rule line 33 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.sdp.md:33
The Studio is write-careful: it writes nothing to canonical source, and a change a person wants leaves it as scoped intent for an agent, as spec:consumers.edit-model states.
rule.noSecondGraph line 34 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.sdp.md:34
The Studio never builds a second graph: every join, claim, delivery fact, derived readiness, floor failure and finding it shows is a value the reader computed when the Studio was built, and the page computes none of them again.

no example exercises it

rule.recipeAnswers line 35 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.sdp.md:35
A page shows a catalog recipe's answer only when the Studio's design names that recipe, and the build composes the answer over the graph it derived; the page recomputes none of it.

no example exercises it

rule.namedInputs line 36 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.sdp.md:36
Beside the graph the Studio reads only two optional inputs, a base graph and run records; each is named on every page that shows it, never becomes graph data, a delivery fact or a verdict, and never answers in the graph's name.

no example exercises it

7 unkeyed rules.

Verification · manual
criteria
  • The Studio is accepted when a person given only a link to a build of the first adopter's corpus completes, from the page set alone, the five tasks the first adopter set over its history-view Pack (libar-platform/docs/feedback/sdp-feedback-01.md): find the history contract, locate OD-157, explain the aggregate dependency, find one declaration's type comparison down to the source line that checks it, and say whether a paused-rebuild example has native-backend evidence. Given no run records, the last task passes when the person finds that the example requires the native backend tier, reads whether a verifier is bound to it, and reports that no run result is supplied.
  • The same person names which statements the owner can make first, from the owner queue page.
  • The same person, given a build with a base graph, names what changed in the design since the base, from the diff page.
  • The same person names which components are designed and not yet built, from the architecture lens.

Design view

Requirement drawing

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.shipped-projections-frozen

    Re-specifying the shipped Design Review, census, Mermaid, or Gherkin projection is refused. These four projections are the ruled read surfaces over the one graph. A later decision Spec that supersedes this one replaces the ruling whole; a decision Spec that refines this one narrows it for one projection or one rendering and leaves the rest frozen. Either passes the ADR three-part test.

  • The build renders every Studio view, and an element only enhances it

    The build renders every Studio view into the page's markup from reader values and the recipe answers its page names, and a custom element adds only the interaction its view needs; a host page that embeds a view carries the markup the build wrote and loads the element script, and supplies no graph data.

  • The Studio renders HTML, and the HTML stays derived

    The Studio renders generated HTML as its surface. The HTML is derived and never committed: git diffs stay over the canonical Spec source, and the Studio's files are regenerated from the graph.

  • The Studio is built from custom elements, not a framework

    The Studio is built from Web Components, custom elements written without React, Vue, Svelte or another framework.

2. The Studio renders HTML, and the HTML stays derived

spec:decisions.studio-html-surface

The Studio renders HTML, and the HTML stays derived

spec:decisions.studio-html-surfaceDecision Record · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/decisions/studio-html-surface.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding none, verifier binding none, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Give reviewers a Studio with search, filters and collapsible views while git diffs stay over canonical Spec source.
Decision
context
When a model writes the Specs, a person's main act is review, and review reads tables, diagrams, code, comparisons and examples across many Specs. The first adopter's reviewers need search, filters, navigation and progressive disclosure across a Pack, which the generated Markdown pages do not give: the Pack page's member table is too wide for those readers, and they open the carrier files instead.
decision
The Studio renders generated HTML as its surface. The HTML is derived and never committed: git diffs stay over the canonical Spec source, and the Studio's files are regenerated from the graph.
rationale
  • HTML conveys more per screen: collapsible sections, wide tables that scroll in place, SVG diagrams, highlighted code and side-by-side comparisons are native to it.
  • HTML is shareable: a page set uploaded to any static host is a link a reviewer opens without installing anything.
  • HTML is interactive: search, filters and navigation run in the page over values the build wrote, which Markdown cannot do.
  • The Studio's code renders its HTML from the graph, so the original's argument from generation time and token cost, which priced a page a model writes, does not apply.
alternatives
  • Markdown renders in Markdown viewers and agents read it as text; the generated Markdown Design Review lacks the Studio's search, filters and collapsible views, so it stays beside the Studio.
consequences
  • The principal trade-off of HTML, diffs that are noisier in git, is sidestepped because the HTML is derived and never committed.
  • The Studio stands beside the Markdown Design Review. The Studio is an interactive workbench, the frozen Markdown Design Review is a generated view for agents and Markdown readers, and git review stays over canonical Spec source; neither view ranks above the other.
  • The case for derived HTML holds for any canonical carrier, because it rests on the HTML being derived and never committed, not on the Specs being written in TypeScript.
  • The richer interactions the original design lists, such as moving a target on a slider, running a scenario harness or reordering members by drag and drop, wait for later phases and their own Specs; the Studio's first build is read-only.

3. The Studio renders from the reader's values and embeds only what its script reads

spec:consumers.spec-studio.data

The Studio renders from the reader's values and embeds only what its script reads

spec:consumers.spec-studio.dataContract · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: 5 design entries · 5 pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The build writes each value into the page's markup, so a page reads in full as HTML. Search is the exception: a browser refuses a fetch from a page opened through file://, so the search page carries its index inside it. On the first adopter's corpus that index is too large to repeat on every page, which is why search runs on a page of its own.

Intent
outcome
Render every Studio page from the values the reader returns for the graph the agent surface reads, so a page derives nothing of its own and carries only the data its script needs.
Contract
rule.readerValues line 24 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.sdp.md:24
The build renders the index from specs(), packs(), findings(), each Spec's design columns and the epic memberships recipe 52 answers, a Pack page from packContext and the Pack totals, a Spec page from specContext, and the search page from the search index; every page's rail renders the rail values. A page states no value the reader did not return or a named recipe did not answer, apart from counts the build takes of those values.

no example exercises it

rule.embeddedData line 25 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.sdp.md:25
A page whose script reads data embeds it in one script element of type application/json with the id sdp-data, serialized as JSON with every < then written as the six characters \u003c, so no text can close the element. The search page embeds the search index there; every other page embeds no data, because its values are in its markup.

no example exercises it

rule.noDataFiles line 26 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.sdp.md:26
The page set writes no data file of its own: an agent reads the graph through sdp q, and sdp build writes the serialized graph.

no example exercises it

rule.noSlices line 27 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.sdp.md:27
The Studio's data holds no context bundle or other AI slice: the context bundle is composed on each invocation and never saved, and a design pass composes one with its recipe when it needs it. A slice page renders the design slice's answer into its markup, as every page renders its values, and embeds no slice data.

no example exercises it

specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.recipe-answers.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The lenses, the registers, the owner queue, the slice and roadmap pages, the diff and runs pages and the panels of a Spec page show recipe answers. Each takes its answer from the recipe's shipped body, evaluated over the graph the build derived, so a page and sdp q give one answer. The two Design entries name every evaluation a build runs and which page reads each answer, so a builder and a test author read one list.

Intent
outcome
Compose every recipe answer a Studio page shows by evaluating the recipe's shipped body over the graph the build derived, so a page and sdp q give one answer.
Contract
rule.recipeEvaluation line 20 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.recipe-answers.sdp.md:20
The build composes each recipe answer a page shows by evaluating that recipe's shipped body, the one dist/recipes/ holds, over the graph, reader and validation report it derived, with the parameters the recipe evaluations name, through the body evaluation sdp q runs; it re-implements no recipe, so a page and sdp q give one answer.

no example exercises it

rule.oncePerBuild line 21 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.recipe-answers.sdp.md:21

recipeEvaluations line 24 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.recipe-answers.sdp.md:24
a build evaluates each of these once, with no parameter unless one is named: recipes 17, 20, 24, 31, 33, 43, 44, 46, 51 and 53; recipe 52 with { detail: true }; recipe 29 with { pack: id } and recipe 54 with { pack: id, detail: true } for every Pack; recipe 55 with { pack: id } for every Pack whose manifest states order: priority; recipe 21 with { spec: id } and recipe 30 with { specs: [id] } for every Spec; recipe 34 with { spec: id } for every Spec that is not an example, Specs in no Pack included; given a base graph, recipe 35 with { base, detail: true }, and with { base, pack: id, detail: true } for every Pack; given run records, recipe 45 with { runs }.
pageRecipes line 25 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.recipe-answers.sdp.md:25
the index renders reader values and each Spec's epicIds from recipe 52; the glossary renders reader values only; the capabilities lens renders recipe 52; the architecture lens renders recipes 17 and 43; the tests lens renders every recipe 34 answer, recipe 44, and recipe 45 given run records; a Spec page renders its recipe 21, 30 and 34 answers, its own space from recipe 44, the recipe 51 rows that cite its entries, the recipe 45 files whose specs hold its id, and its own row of recipe 35's whole-corpus answer; a Pack page renders the totals of its recipe 29 answer and, given a base graph, its own recipe 35 answer; a slice page renders its Pack's recipe 54 answer; the roadmap page renders recipe 53 and each roadmap's recipe 55 memo; the registers render recipes 20, 31, 24 beside recipe 51's rows, and 33; the owner queue renders recipe 46; the diff page renders recipe 35's whole-corpus answer; the runs page renders recipe 45; an export renders the values of the pages it holds.

5. The Studio reads two named inputs beside the graph, a base graph and run records

spec:consumers.spec-studio.data.inputs

The Studio reads two named inputs beside the graph, a base graph and run records

spec:consumers.spec-studio.data.inputsContract · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: 2 design entries · 2 pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.inputs.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

Two inputs may ride beside the graph: the graph an earlier commit wrote, so a page can show what changed since, and CI run records, so a reviewer reads what ran beside the verifier bindings. Each is named on the command line and on every page that shows it, and neither answers in the graph's name. Without them the page set is what the graph alone writes.

Intent
outcome
Let the Studio's build read a base graph and run records beside the graph, each named where it shows, while the graph alone writes the page set when neither is given.
Contract
rule.namedInputs line 25 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.inputs.sdp.md:25
Beside the graph the build reads at most two inputs, each named on the command line: a base graph, the graph object sdp build wrote at an earlier commit, which reaches recipe 35 as params.base; and run records, each one Common Test Report Format document, which reach recipe 45 as params.runs. The build reads neither in any other way.

spec:consumers.spec-studio.data.inputs.both-given · enabled, spec:consumers.spec-studio.data.inputs.graph-only · enabled

rule.inputFlags line 26 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.inputs.sdp.md:26
The studio verb also takes --base PATH, naming the base graph, a JSON file sdp build wrote; --base-label TEXT, the words that name the base graph on its pages; and --runs PATH, naming one run record, a JSON file in the Common Test Report Format, repeatable, the records keeping the order of their flags. --base-label without --base, or --base given twice, is refused.

spec:consumers.spec-studio.data.inputs.both-given · enabled

rule.inputPlacement line 27 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.inputs.sdp.md:27
Before extraction or output cleanup, the command refuses an input path that the build could write or remove, including a path beneath a projection root and an alias resolving to such a path; it reports the flag and path, exits 1 and changes no file.

no example exercises it

rule.unreadableInput line 28 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.inputs.sdp.md:28
An input file that cannot be read or does not hold JSON refuses the run before extraction, with exit 1 and one line on stderr naming the flag and the path; a JSON value a recipe cannot read shows on its page as that recipe's diagnostics.

no example exercises it

rule.inputPages line 29 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.inputs.sdp.md:29
An input adds pages and page sections, never a data file: the base graph adds diff.html and the changed-since-base sections of the Spec and Pack pages, and run records add runs.html and the run rows of the tests lens and the verification panels.

spec:consumers.spec-studio.data.inputs.both-given · enabled, spec:consumers.spec-studio.data.inputs.graph-only · enabled

rule.inputNaming line 30 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.inputs.sdp.md:30
A page that shows an input names it in words, the base graph by its label when it was given one, its schema version and its Spec count, and a run as spec:consumers.spec-studio.runs-page names it; no page holds an input's path.

spec:consumers.spec-studio.data.inputs.both-given · enabled

rule.inputsNeverGraph line 31 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.inputs.sdp.md:31
An input never becomes graph data, a delivery fact, a finding, a rung or a verdict: no page counts a run toward a binding, and no difference from the base moves a rung.

spec:consumers.spec-studio.data.inputs.both-given · enabled

rule.sameInputsSameBytes line 33 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.data.inputs.sdp.md:33
Without inputs the page set is the one the graph alone writes; with them, the same graph and the same input bytes and labels write the same page set, byte for byte, and a value an input carries, such as a run's commit and times, shows only on the pages that name that input.

8. sdp studio publishes the Studio as one page set

spec:consumers.spec-studio.publisher

sdp studio publishes the Studio as one page set

spec:consumers.spec-studio.publisherUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The Studio has its own verb and root beside the four shipped publishers, and is written the way they are. Its page set opens from the file system and uploads to a static host unchanged. The run adds no stamp, commit or time, so two runs over one graph write the same bytes, and a publishing step that wants build context writes its stamp beside the page set.

Intent
outcome
Publish the Studio under its own root as one page set the graph and its named inputs alone determine, which opens through file:// and uploads to a static host unchanged.
Behavior
rule.verb line 25 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.sdp.md:25
sdp studio [root] [--exclude PATH]... [--check-clean] validates the graph and writes the Studio's page set to <root>/generated/spec-studio/; root defaults to the working directory, and each exclusion is a root-relative path prefix, as for the shipped publishers.

no example exercises it

rule.ownRoot line 26 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.sdp.md:26
A run writes nothing outside its root, writes no stamp, and leaves every carrier and source file under the root byte-identical.

no example exercises it

rule.readsNoNetwork line 27 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.sdp.md:27
A run reads no network: every byte it reads is a file under the root, a file its flags name, or a file the package ships.

no example exercises it

rule.wholesale line 28 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.sdp.md:28
A run writes its page set to generated/spec-studio.tmp/, removes the prior root and renames the temporary into place, so no page of an earlier run survives a later one and no temporary survives a completed run.

no example exercises it

rule.buildInvalidates line 29 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.sdp.md:29
Every command that enters the shared build, sdp studio among them, removes generated/spec-studio/ and its temporary sibling before extraction, beside the four roots spec:consumers.wholesale-view-rewrite names; a removal failure refuses the command before extraction.

no example exercises it

Cited at

  • test/skills.test.ts:1693
rule.checkClean line 30 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.sdp.md:30
sdp studio --check-clean renders an independent twin and refuses divergent renders, then compares the current root with the new render; missing or drifted output returns nonzero and is removed, and clean output is replaced wholesale with byte-identical content.

no example exercises it

rule.findingsShown line 31 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.sdp.md:31
Findings never withhold the page set: a run over a graph with validation findings still publishes and returns the validation exit code, and each finding shows on the index, and also on its subject's page when its subject is a Spec or a Pack. A run whose extraction fails publishes nothing and returns nonzero.

no example exercises it

rule.pageSet line 32 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.sdp.md:32
The page set holds index.html, search.html, one packs/<name>.html and one slices/<name>.html per Pack, one specs/<name>.html per Spec, and assets/studio.css and assets/studio.js. <name> is the id after its namespace, with each uppercase ASCII letter written as _ and its lowercase, so no two pages collide on a file system that ignores case.

no example exercises it

rule.deterministic line 33 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.sdp.md:33
Two runs over one graph and the same inputs write byte-identical files, and no file holds a time, a commit, an absolute path or a host name of the run's own.

no example exercises it

rule.linksResolve line 34 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.sdp.md:34
Every link a page writes stays inside the page set: it resolves to a page the run wrote and, with a fragment, to an element id that page carries, apart from the search page's term fragment search.html#q=<term>, which names no element. No page links a carrier or source file, an editor URI or an external address; the only link that leaves the page set is one the stamp element adds in the browser from a present stamp's source template.

Design view

Requirement drawing

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.shipped-projections-frozen

    Re-specifying the shipped Design Review, census, Mermaid, or Gherkin projection is refused. These four projections are the ruled read surfaces over the one graph. A later decision Spec that supersedes this one replaces the ruling whole; a decision Spec that refines this one narrows it for one projection or one rendering and leaves the rest frozen. Either passes the ADR three-part test.

9. sdp studio --watch rebuilds the page set on each carrier change

spec:consumers.spec-studio.publisher.watch

sdp studio --watch rebuilds the page set on each carrier change

spec:consumers.spec-studio.publisher.watchUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.watch.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

While an author edits, the watch rebuilds the page set on each carrier change, and a person reloads the page to read it. Each cycle writes exactly what a plain run with the same arguments writes, so the watch adds no server, no live reload and no script of its own.

Intent
outcome
Rebuild the Studio's page set on every carrier change while an author edits, each cycle byte for byte what a plain run writes, with no server and no injected script.
Behavior
rule.watch line 20 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.publisher.watch.sdp.md:20
sdp studio --watch installs the carrier watcher validate's watch installs, publishes once at start and again after every carrier create, change, delete or rename, each cycle writing the page set a plain sdp studio with the same arguments writes, byte for byte; it serves no page and injects no script, so a reader reloads to read the new build. Findings print each cycle and the process stays alive; a cycle whose extraction fails removes the page set; operator SIGINT exits 0; edits to source files and input files start no cycle; --watch cannot combine with --check-clean.

The Studio's shell frames every page with navigation, a rail and a canvas

spec:consumers.spec-studio.shellUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The shell carries what every page shares, including the rules that keep a page readable: by keyboard, without color, on a phone and without its script. Recent edits stay out of it, because a page is a function of the graph alone and git holds the history.

Intent
outcome
Let a person move between the index, Packs and Specs from any page, find a Spec by what they remember of it, and read every page by keyboard, on a phone and without its script.
Behavior
rule line 27 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:27
Every page has the same shell: a top navigation, a left rail and a main canvas, and it opens with a link that skips to the canvas.
rule line 28 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:28
A search field is on every page; spec:consumers.spec-studio.search states what it matches and how its results show.
rule line 29 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:29
The rail's count of findings is the count of the validation report's findings, never a count the page derives.
rule.noRecentEdits line 30 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:30
The shell shows no recent edits and no other history: git holds it.

no example exercises it

rule.stamp line 31 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:31
Served over http or https, the shell reads stamp.json beside the page set and, when it loads, shows the build context it names; a page opened through file:// requests nothing and shows no stamp.

no example exercises it

rule.rungBadge line 32 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:32
A stated rung shows as a badge that carries the rung's word, colored from a palette of four that stays distinct under color blindness; the floor reached shows beside it as words with no color of its own, and only the divergence banner adds a warning color, beside its words.

no example exercises it

rule.wordsBesideColor line 33 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:33
Every meaning a color conveys is also written in words, so no reading depends on color.

no example exercises it

rule.keyboard line 34 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:34
Every link and control is reachable from the keyboard in reading order and shows where the focus is.

no example exercises it

rule.lineLength line 35 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:35
Prose runs no wider than about 80 characters, and a table wider than the canvas scrolls inside its own box, never the page.

no example exercises it

rule.text line 36 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:36
Authored text renders as plain text with each inline code span as code, and no other Markdown is read. A mention the prose-mentions validator reads links to its target's page when the target resolves, and to the entry when the mention is an entry address.

no example exercises it

rule.withoutScript line 37 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:37
Every page but the search page reads in full without its script: its collapsible parts are native disclosure elements, and only filtering, copying, the stamp, pan and zoom, and the composing panel need the script. The search page needs its script to match, and without it says so and links to the index.

no example exercises it

UI

The parts of the shell, top to bottom and left to right.

topNavigation line 41 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:41
the Studio's name linking to the index, then Packs, linking to the index's Packs section, then the search field; each lens page the page set holds adds its entry in the order spec:consumers.spec-studio.lenses gives.
stampLine line 42 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:42
at the end of the top navigation, the stamp's corpus commit, engine and build time, when the stamp loads.
leftRail line 43 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:43
on a Pack page, the Pack's members in authored order, each linked to its card on the page; on a Spec page, each Pack the Spec belongs to with its members in authored order, each linked to its Spec page and the current one marked; on any other page, every Pack; then, on a Pack or Spec page, under an Example spaces heading shown only when there is one, each member of the rail's Packs that owns an example space, linked to its Spec page, with no harness named; then the validation report's finding counts by severity, linked to the index's findings.
railOnPhone line 44 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:44
below the phone breakpoint the rail follows the canvas, so a page opens on its content.
mainCanvas line 45 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.shell.sdp.md:45
the page of the Spec or Pack selected in the rail or in a lens.

12. Search finds a Spec, a Pack, an entry or a bound file by a word

spec:consumers.spec-studio.search

Search finds a Spec, a Pack, an entry or a bound file by a word

spec:consumers.spec-studio.searchUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: 6 design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The first adopter asked to search entry keys, pinned declarations and file paths. A Spec's envelope holds no tags, so search reads what the graph holds: the fields concept search reads, which already include every pinned declaration, plus the keys authors coin and the files the graph records. The page matches with the reader's own code, so a term finds on the page what findByConcept finds through sdp q.

Intent
outcome
Let a person find a Spec, a Pack, a keyed entry or the code bound at a file by a word they remember of it, from any page and with no request.
Behavior
rule.oneMatcher line 21 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:21
Search matches with the reader's concept matching, one implementation the package exports without Node dependencies and the page script bundles, so over the fields findByConcept reads, the page returns the nodes it returns, in its order.

no example exercises it

rule.addedFields line 22 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:22
Search also matches the keys authors coin, Design and UI keys, open question keys and rule keys, and a node's recorded file path; a node matched only through these follows every node findByConcept matches, in id order. It indexes nothing else.

no example exercises it

rule line 23 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:23
A term matches where it appears in a field, without regard to case, as findByConcept matches; an empty term matches nothing.
rule.searchPage line 24 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:24
The search field on any page opens the search page with the term in its fragment, search.html#q=<term>; the search page matches as the person types and keeps the term in its fragment, so a search is a link.

no example exercises it

rule.resultShape line 25 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:25
Each result names its node type in words. A Spec result shows its title, id, kind, and stated rung beside the floor reached, and opens its page; a Pack result shows its title and id and opens its page, with no readiness; an Anchor or CodeNode result shows its id, label, and recorded file and line as text with a copy action, and links each Spec its edges reach, with the edge type.

no example exercises it

rule.entryHits line 26 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:26
A Spec with a matching entry is a result. Under a Spec result, the page lists the Spec's entries the term matches, as spec:consumers.spec-studio.data#design.searchEntry states, in the index's order, each with its section, key and recorded line, linked to the entry's element id on the Spec page when it has an entry address, and otherwise to its section's element id, or to the narrative's.

no example exercises it

rule line 27 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:27
The page shows fifty results at a time, with a control that shows the next fifty.
rule line 28 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:28
The search page reads only the index it embeds; it fetches nothing and joins nothing.

3 unkeyed rules.

UI
searchField line 31 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:31
a labelled text field and a Search button in the top navigation of every page.
resultsHeader line 32 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:32
the term, how many nodes and entries match, and the fields searched.
resultCard line 33 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:33
one card per node, in result order: its node type in words, title and id, the fields that matched, and the Spec's rungs or the unit's location as the result rule states; then its entry hits.
entryHit line 34 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:34
one line per entry: its section, its key as code, its recorded line, and the text around the term, shortened.
noMatch line 35 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:35
No node matches and the term, then the fields searched.
needsScript line 36 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.search.sdp.md:36
without script, the search page says that search needs it and links to the index.

specs/consumers/spec-studio.navigation.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The shell's top navigation reaches the index and each lens, and the index routes a reader by the task they came to do. The register pages, the owner queue, the glossary, and the diff and runs pages join both, so a reviewer with only a link reaches every page from any page and sees which page they are on.

Intent
outcome
Let a person reach every page of the page set from the top navigation of any page, and from the index by the task they came to do.
Behavior
rule.topEntries line 24 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.navigation.sdp.md:24
After the lens entries, the top navigation lists Roadmap, Queue, Questions, Decisions, Declarations, Backlog and Glossary, then Diff when the build was given a base graph and Runs when it was given run records, each linking its page; the search field follows them.

no example exercises it

rule.currentPage line 25 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.navigation.sdp.md:25
The top-navigation link to the page being read carries aria-current="page" and an underline, so it shows by more than color.

Five lenses read the graph as Packs, capabilities, architecture, tests and evidence

specs/consumers/spec-studio.lenses.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Each lens is a page with a Spec of its own, so each builds on the graph it reads today: the Packs, capabilities, architecture and tests lenses read what the graph records, and the evidence lens reads not tracked until the graph records an observation. This Spec keeps what the five share.

Intent
outcome
Let a person see the graph five ways, by Pack, by capability, by architecture, by verification and by evidence, from one top navigation.
Behavior
rule.order line 18 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.lenses.sdp.md:18
The lenses are pages of the page set, reached from the top navigation in the order Packs, capabilities, architecture, tests, evidence; the index page is the Packs lens and the default landing page.

specs/consumers/spec-studio.index-page.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

A reader of a large design needs two ways in: by the task they came to do and by a word they remember. The index gives the first and links to search for the second, opens with a summary the build counts, and replaces one long table with a list a person narrows.

Intent
outcome
Give a person one landing page that says where the corpus stands, routes them by task, lists every Pack with its members, and narrows every Spec by the coordinates and bindings they ask about.

17. The architecture lens draws components by context and layer, the planned beside the built

spec:consumers.spec-studio.lenses.architecture

The architecture lens draws components by context and layer, the planned beside the built

spec:consumers.spec-studio.lenses.architectureUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

specs/consumers/spec-studio.lenses.architecture.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

The original's architecture lens drew runtime layers, ports and external systems beside components. The graph holds what the architectural annotation decision admits: a component anchor's layer and bounded context, any unit's role, membership and uses, and no port or external-system node. So the lens groups components by their recorded context and layer and draws membership and uses only. A design ahead of its code states its components in component designs, which no anchor realizes yet; the lens draws them in the same grid, marked planned, so a reader sees what is designed and not built where it will sit.

Intent
outcome
Let a person see the components the code realizes and the components the design plans, grouped by bounded context and layer, with what each uses and what it holds.
Behavior

Beside the architecture drawing comes the component uses table, read from recipe 17's component rows and their counts of unit uses edges: one row per realized component as the user and one column per realized component as the used. A nonzero cell holds the count of anchored unit uses edges behind the pair and links to that use in the row component's detail; a zero cell between two components shows ·, with no anchored use recorded as hidden text and the legend · means no anchored use recorded, and the cell where a component meets itself stays empty. Planned uses, unresolved endpoints and uses within one component stay in their own readings and never enter the table. The table is not a drawing, and it reads in full without script and in print.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.architectural-annotation

    Architectural significance is annotated on the anchor of the unit that realizes it. A code anchor may carry role, the architectural pattern the unit plays; a component: anchor may additionally carry layer, one of edge, application, domain, adapter, or infrastructure, and context, its bounded context. The component: anchor is anchored architecture: it is the declared component, and there is no separate architecture file, because the anchor sits where the component is realized. It is not the original design's declared Component that could exist before code; an unrealized component lives in Specs and never as an invented CodeNode. A role is a free, corpus-owned vocabulary whose taxonomy the census renders with counts from the graph; service, decider, projection, read-model, codec, contract, barrel, and utility are the lineage set, not a closed list. layer is a closed set, and a value outside it is an envelope error; layer or context on a non-component anchor is an envelope error. All three attributes are optional, and omission is lawful.

specs/consumers/spec-studio.lenses.tests.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

A verifier binding states that a verifier exists, and pass and fail stay in CI, so the lens shows bindings and coverage. It shows a run result only when the build was given run records, and then as evidence from a test file, never as a verdict on a Spec.

Intent
outcome
Let a person see, for every Spec, whether a verifier is bound, which keyed rules an example exercises, and which example-space values no example binds.
Behavior
rule.coverageRows line 27 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.lenses.tests.sdp.md:27
The lens lists one row per Spec that is not an example, in id order: its verifier binding as present or none, with its verifiers and how many are enabled; its keyed rules with how many an enabled example exercises, from recipe 34; its unkeyed rules, counted apart because the graph cannot tell which examples exercise a rule with no key; and, when it owns an example space, its uncovered values and the examples that leave a slot unbound, from recipe 44. Each row links to the verification panel of the Spec's page. A space with no enumerable slot is not measurable, whether or not it has examples; otherwise it is uncovered when any enumerable value has no example and covered when all enumerable values have examples. Non-enumerable slots do not affect a mixed space's classification.

specs/consumers/agent-surface.example-space-coverage.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

The original design rendered a coverage heatmap from each example space: which combinations of its typed slots an example witnesses and which none does (docs/lineage/v0-design/04-authoring-surfaces.md §4 and §4.1, 06-extraction-and-validation.md §8). This Spec reports slot-value coverage; the glossary keeps witness for an example in an outcome class. Coverage is per slot value: no design pass has yet asked which combinations of slots no example exercises, and a combination grid grows with the product of the slots' sizes.

Intent
problem
The graph carries example spaces and bound points, but no reader value or recipe reports which literal slot values example children bind.
outcome

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding none, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Execute per-value coverage on a closed union with one covered, two uncovered values and one child that binds nothing.
assumptions
  • The world writes a parent Spec whose example space declares the slot as a closed union of the literals the declared value lists, separated by |, and one example child per entry of the bound value, separated by ; , each child refining and verifying the parent and binding that literal, or binding no value where the entry is none; it runs recipe 44's shipped body with the parent as spec and joins the uncovered values and the unbound children's ids with , . The parent's id ends in probe.parent, and each child's id is the parent's followed by .c1, .c2 and on, in order.
Behavior

Examples

Given an example space that declares the slot {slot: "availability"} as {declared: "in stock|out of stock|backordered"}
Given its example children bind {bound: "in stock; in stock; none"}
When recipe 44 reports the space's coverage
Then the slot is enumerable: {enumerable: true}
Then the values no example binds are {uncovered: "out of stock, backordered"}
Then the examples that leave the slot unbound are {unbound: "spec:probe.parent.c3"}

specs/consumers/spec-studio.pack-page.maturity-map.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

A Pack's maturity map shows its distribution before its member lists. Equal-sized cells place each resolved member by stated readiness and floor reached. Populated cells show exact counts and member marks; faint empty cells show no number. The count table and ordered lists retain the reading in text.

Intent
outcome
Let a reviewer see at a glance where every member of a Pack stands, by the rung it states and the floor it reaches.
Behavior

Every resolved member belongs to one stated-rung and floor cell; unresolved members are named apart. Populated cells link to their built lists, whose members stay in authored order.

specs/consumers/spec-studio.spec-page.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

The original runtime panel linked Fastify routes to Effect programs, showed what Effect layers provided and required, and recorded Awilix registrations and their lifetimes, beside ports and external systems. That representation is lineage evidence in docs/lineage/v0-design/07-spec-studio-and-projections.md, section 2.3, Section F. The structural anchors record identity, component membership, uses, role, and a component's architectural layer and context, so the runtime panel shows that structural neighborhood and no more until a reader asks for more of the runtime composition.

The page shows only what the graph and the build's named inputs hold. The original header's owner, tags and last-verified time, its schema bindings and its UI / Stories section have no graph value behind them, so the page shows none of them.

Intent
outcome
Show everything the graph holds about one Spec on one page, in panels a person opens and closes one at a time.
Behavior
rule line 42 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.spec-page.sdp.md:42
Each panel collapses and expands on its own.
rule line 43 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.spec-page.sdp.md:43

rule.sourceText line 44 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.spec-page.sdp.md:44
Every Spec and Pack a panel names links to its page. A code unit, component or anchor shows its id and its recorded repository-relative file and line as text, with an action that copies file:line; the page set holds no code-unit page and writes no editor URI, absolute path or assumed source URL; a recorded file and line become a link only when a stamp beside the page set names a source template, as spec:consumers.spec-studio.sharing states; a component's attributes, members and uses show in the architecture lens, which its id links to.

Design view

Requirement drawing

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.authored-entry-order

    The Design Review renders each entry of a design or ui section as a list item in authored order, its key as inline code. A string value renders as Markdown text through the prose escaping rule; a number or boolean renders as inline code; an array or object renders as a fenced JSON block nested under its item, so a structured value the TypeScript carrier admits survives without loss. The fenced-JSON rule of the Design Review stops covering an open section as a whole and keeps covering a structured value inside one entry. The freeze on the four shipped projections stands for everything else.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.authored-entry-order

    The Design Review renders each entry of a design or ui section as a list item in authored order, its key as inline code. A string value renders as Markdown text through the prose escaping rule; a number or boolean renders as inline code; an array or object renders as a fenced JSON block nested under its item, so a structured value the TypeScript carrier admits survives without loss. The fenced-JSON rule of the Design Review stops covering an open section as a whole and keeps covering a structured value inside one entry. The freeze on the four shipped projections stands for everything else.

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

The graph records that a verifier binding exists and never a run, and a static page runs nothing, so the panels show bindings and offer no run of an example. A run result shows only when the build was given run records, and then as evidence from a test file. No Spec designs a source for build attestations, deployments or bills of materials, so each reads not tracked. Moving a constraint target on a slider and running a scenario harness wait for designs of their own, as the HTML surface decision records; a panel action composes intent instead.

33. The corpus's registers are pages a reviewer opens from a link

spec:consumers.spec-studio.registers

The corpus's registers are pages a reviewer opens from a link

spec:consumers.spec-studio.registersUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

specs/consumers/spec-studio.registers.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

A large design keeps registers, and each is a catalog recipe an agent runs. Four become pages, so a reviewer with only a link reads the same rows: the open questions and the decisions, which the owner works through; the pinned declarations, each with the source lines that cite it, which is where a reader finds the test that checks a declaration; and the design backlog, the Specs designed and not yet built, which a design ahead of its code is mostly made of. The key-family register stays a recipe: its rows depend on key prefixes a corpus chooses, the Studio takes no corpus configuration, and search already finds a coined key.

Intent
outcome
Let a person read every open question, decision, pinned declaration and designed-but-unbuilt Spec of the corpus on one page each, linked to the entries they name.
Behavior

The owner queue page orders the statements and questions only a person can settle

specs/consumers/spec-studio.owner-queue.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

A large design waits on one person: the statements its floor already allows and the questions only its owner decides. The readiness planner orders those statements, the ones they rest on first. This page shows that order to a reviewer with only a link, so the owner sees which statements can be made first and which questions hold the most. A rung stays a person's statement, so the page orders and links and states nothing.

Intent
outcome
Let the owner see, in one place, every statement the floor allows in the order that holds, and every open question only the owner settles, blocking ones first.

Iterating on a design asks what changed since the last pass, or what a change proposal would change. specs/consumers/spec-studio.runs-page.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

CI keeps the results of its test runs; the graph records only that a verifier is bound. Given run records in the Common Test Report Format, the build shows each run and the test files it joins, so a reviewer reads what ran where the verifiers are anchored. A result is evidence from a file, never the verdict of one verifier, and never a delivery fact.

Intent
outcome
Let a person read, from a link, the test runs the build was given, which anchored test files each joins, and which records join none, each labelled as external evidence.

41. CI run records are joined to verifiers in a view

spec:observation.run-evidence

CI run records are joined to verifiers in a view

spec:observation.run-evidenceUse Case / Behavior · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: 7 design entries · 5 pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md

1 open question and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

The original design put test reports in the graph and used passing runs to mark verification. The Protocol keeps run verdicts in CI. A resolving verifier binding confers has-verifier; showing a recorded run beside that binding confers no delivery fact. Runtime observation against a measurable target is a separate concern carried by the runtime overlay.

An adopter that keeps CI run reports needs to read them beside verifier bindings as a separately named input. Recipe 45 reads them, and the Studio admits them as one of its two named inputs. The view identifies each run by its own fields and its commit, and distinguishes evidence from a test file from a verdict for one anchored verifier. Test reporters write a test's file as an absolute path or a path from the directory they ran in, so the join reads a path's end as well as the whole path. The freshness question records what remains unsettled about comparing a run with the source being read.

Intent
problem
A reader who wants to know whether a bound verifier passed has to leave the Protocol's views for CI, and an adopter that keeps run records has no view that shows them beside the binding without mistaking them for a delivery fact.
outcome
Show a verifier's recorded runs beside its binding in a view, labelled as external input with its commit, while the graph keeps recording only that the binding exists.

Open questions

  • non-blocking · question.freshness line 28 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:28 · How does a view say a run is stale: by its commit against the commit being read, or by whether the bound files changed between the two?Decider: ownerProvisional: Display the run and source commit identifiers when they differ, as the differing-commit rule requires; whether freshness also follows changes to bound files remains open.
Behavior
rule.graphUntouched line 33 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:33
Run records are an input a view reads beside the graph, named by the caller; the graph never holds them, and no node, edge or delivery fact derives from them.

spec:observation.run-evidence.absolute-path-joins · enabled, spec:observation.run-evidence.unanchored-file-unjoined · enabled

rule.fileGrain line 34 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:34
A run record joins every verifier whose test anchor sits in the test file the record names, because the file is the binding grain of both anchor forms; each test name in the record shows as a row under that verifier. The join is at file grain: a result is evidence from the verifier's file, never the result of that verifier, because a file may hold several suites and a filtered run may exercise only one.

spec:observation.run-evidence.absolute-path-joins · enabled

rule.ctrfInput line 35 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:35
The Protocol reads run records in the Common Test Report Format, CTRF, an open JSON schema with reporters for the common test runners, passed to a view as a recipe parameter. A record joins only when its reporter fills CTRF's optional filePath field, and an adopter with records of another shape maps them into CTRF itself.

spec:observation.run-evidence.absolute-path-joins · enabled

rule.pathNormalization line 36 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:36
A record's file path joins a test anchor's file when, with each backslash written as a slash and a leading ./ removed, it equals that file or ends with a slash followed by that file; when several anchored files match, the longest joins.

spec:observation.run-evidence.absolute-path-joins · enabled

rule.unjoinedReported line 37 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:37
A record that names no file path, or a file that holds no test anchor, is reported as unjoined with its reason, never dropped, and an input that is not a CTRF report is reported with its problem while the other inputs still join.

spec:observation.run-evidence.unanchored-file-unjoined · enabled

rule.commitField line 38 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:38
A run's commit is CTRF's results.environment.commit, and a run without one reads not recorded; given the commit being read, the recipe says for each run whether its commit is that commit, and never says the run is fresh or stale.

no example exercises it

rule line 39 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:39
A view shows each run beside the verifiers anchored in its file, with its result, its commit and the input it came from, labelled as external run evidence from that file and never as has-verifier, implemented or a pass verdict for one verifier.
rule line 40 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:40
A run whose commit differs from the commit being read shows both commits, so a reader sees how old it is.
rule.studioInput line 41 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:41
The Design Review stays a function of the graph alone and shows no run; run evidence appears only in a view that explicitly admits records as external input: recipe 45, and the Studio built with run records, which shows them on its runs page, in its tests lens and on the Spec pages of the Specs their files verify.

runsRecipe line 44 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:44
recipe 45, run evidence, takes params.runs, one CTRF report or a list of them in input order, required; params.commit, the commit being read, optional; and params.spec, a Spec id, optional, which keeps only the files whose test anchors verify that Spec directly or through an enabled example. It returns { inputs, diagnostics, totals, files, unjoined }, and { diagnostics } alone when params.runs is missing or holds no report it can read.
ctrfFields line 45 · specs/observation/run-evidence.sdp.md:45
the recipe reads reportFormat and specVersion; results.tool.name and version; results.summary with tests, passed, failed, skipped, pending, other, start and stop; results.environment with commit, branchName, buildName and buildNumber; and per test name, status, duration, filePath and suite; it reads no other field. A readable CTRF report has reportFormat: "CTRF" and a specVersion, as the CTRF schema requires; a report missing either produces a run diagnostic and contributes no run rows.

specs/consumers/spec-studio.glossary-page.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

A Spec's Model section defines terms, and a term may carry a key that gives it an address. The glossary page gathers every defined term on one page so a reviewer finds a word and the Spec that defines it. A corpus's ratified glossary stays the document it is; the page lists what the Specs define, so two definitions of one word read side by side.

Intent
outcome
Let a person find any term a Spec defines, read its definition, and open the Spec and the entry that define it.
Behavior

The page set holds glossary.html, which lists every term a Spec's Model section defines, sorted by the term's lowercase form in code-unit order and then by Spec id, each with its definition as text, its Spec linked, and, when the term carries a key, its address spec:<id>#term.<key> with a copy action, linked to the term on the Spec page; the term and its definition split as spec:carrier.markdown-body-grammar states.

46. A composing panel on every page gathers scoped intent for an agent

spec:consumers.spec-studio.intent-panel

A composing panel on every page gathers scoped intent for an agent

spec:consumers.spec-studio.intent-panelUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: 9 design entries · 3 pinned declarations · no decisions

specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

The change-proposal contract requires the commit whose graph the person read, and a generated page set carries no commit, so a proposal's base comes from the build stamp when one is present and from the person otherwise. The panel hands off the same Markdown memo an agent gets from recipe 49 for the same proposal, so a person, a reviewer and an agent read one text. A static page holds no credentials, so the panel opens no pull request and writes nothing but its own gathered intents in the browser.

Intent
outcome
Let a person gather the changes they want while they read, each bounded by a Spec, its neighbors, a Pack or one open question, and hand them to an agent that edits source.
Behavior
rule.everyPage line 24 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.sdp.md:24
The composing panel is on every page, after the canvas, closed by default with its heading and the count of gathered intents; without script it says that composing needs the script.

no example exercises it

rule line 25 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.sdp.md:25
The panel writes no source; its hand-off follows spec:consumers.intent-composition.
rule line 26 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.sdp.md:26
A person gathers intents across pages before handing them off.
rule.persist line 27 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.sdp.md:27
Gathered intents persist in the browser's local storage under the page set's own key, so refreshing a tab on a phone loses none, and two page sets served from one host never share intents.

spec:consumers.spec-studio.intent-panel.refresh-keeps-intents · enabled

rule line 28 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.sdp.md:28
A composed intent names its scope by id or entry address, so the agent that receives it reads the same Spec, Pack, entry or question through the graph.
rule.handOff line 29 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.sdp.md:29
The panel hands its gathered intents off as one change proposal, on the change-proposal contract, and as the memo recipe 49 renders for it: the person copies the memo or the proposal as text, or saves either as a file. The page opens no pull request, because a static page holds no credentials; any pull request comes from the agent's ordinary source edit.

no example exercises it

rule.sameMemo line 30 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.sdp.md:30
The memo the panel writes for a proposal is byte for byte the memo recipe 49 returns for the same proposal.

no example exercises it

rule.proposalBase line 31 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.sdp.md:31
A proposal's base is the commit a present build stamp names, otherwise one the person supplies, and the person gives one reason for the whole proposal; without a base and a reason the panel exports its intents as scoped-intent text, and the agent that receives them writes the proposal against a commit it knows.

no example exercises it

rule.packScope line 32 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.sdp.md:32
A request scoped to a Pack records the members this page set renders for that Pack, and expands to them at hand-off only when the proposal's base is the commit the page set's stamp names; otherwise it stays scoped-intent text for an agent to resolve against the base. A request that changes a Pack's membership or framing, names an empty Pack or names a Pack with an unresolved member, stays scoped-intent text too, so the change-proposal contract keeps its Spec and entry scopes.

no example exercises it

rule.textApart line 33 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.sdp.md:33
The proposal holds only the intents its contract can carry; every intent that stays scoped-intent text is listed apart under Not in the proposal, and Copy scoped intent copies those intents, so the panel drops none. The copied text names each intent's action and recorded scope: the member Spec ids for a member change, with the Pack id as context, or the Pack id for a membership or framing change.

specs/consumers/spec-studio.intent-panel.refresh-keeps-intents.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding none, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Execute the panel's persistence across a refresh of the tab.
assumptions
  • The world runs the composing panel's element module under Node with a storage object standing in for the browser's local storage, gathers the intents through the panel's own gather call, then creates a fresh panel over the same storage and page root, as a refreshed tab would, and counts the intents it shows.

48. Recipe 49 renders a change proposal as the Markdown memo a person reviews

spec:consumers.intent-composition.proposal.memo

Recipe 49 renders a change proposal as the Markdown memo a person reviews

spec:consumers.intent-composition.proposal.memoContract · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: 5 design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.memo.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

A person reviews a proposed change as text, not as JSON beside the proposal check's rows. The memo is a rendering of the proposal document and never a second source of it: it ends with the document itself, so one paste hands an agent everything the person reviewed. Recipe 49 renders it, and the Studio's composing panel writes the same bytes, so a person, a reviewer and an agent read one text.

Intent
outcome
Render a change proposal as one Markdown memo, the same bytes from the recipe and from the Studio's composing panel, that a person reviews and hands to an agent whole.
Contract
rule.memo line 17 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.memo.sdp.md:17

memoChange line 22 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.memo.sdp.md:22
each change follows in document order as the line ## Change <n>, counting from 1, and a blank line, then each on its own line: Scope: followed by the scope items as code spans joined by , ; Request: followed by a blank line and the request in a fenced block whose info string is text; when present, Replaces: or Follows: followed by the address as a code span; Relation: followed by the action, the source as a code span, the relation type and the target as a code span, separated by single spaces; and Reason: followed by the change's reason as a code span; then, when the change carries exact text, a blank line and the text in a fenced block with no info string; then a blank line.

Cited at

  • Test line · test/studio-s5.test.ts:1076 · test:protocol.studio-memo-shared
memoMarkup line 24 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.memo.sdp.md:24
a code span uses a backtick run one longer than the longest run its content holds, padded with a space on each side when the content starts or ends with a backtick; a fence is a backtick run one longer than the longest run its content holds and at least three long; each request and each change's exact text is enclosed in a fence longer than any backtick run it holds, each reason is enclosed in a code span whose backtick run is longer than any run it holds, so no field of the memo can open HTML, add a heading or close its enclosing span or fence; every value is written verbatim; every line ends with a line feed and the memo with one.

outcome

assumptions

Then the memo ends with the proposal as JSON in a fenced block: {carriesDocument: true}
Then the fence around that exact text is {fence: 4} backticks long

The original's harness element has no subject in the graph, which holds example spaces, bound points and oracle bindings but no harness node, so its successor takes the Spec that owns an example space. The build renders every view into the page's markup and an element adds only the interaction its view needs, as spec:decisions.studio-build-renders rules, so a trace graph draws one hop, a maturity map places members by stated rung and floor, a card always shows its rung, and the attributes the original used to choose another setting are gone.

Intent
outcome
Give the Studio a small set of custom elements that each hold one view of the graph, rendered by the build, in a Studio page or in any HTML page that holds that markup and loads the element script.

Design view

Requirement drawing

Decisions

  • The build renders every Studio view, and an element only enhances it

    The build renders every Studio view into the page's markup from reader values and the recipe answers its page names, and a custom element adds only the interaction its view needs; a host page that embeds a view carries the markup the build wrote and loads the element script, and supplies no graph data.

  • The engine lays out every Studio diagram as static SVG when the page set is built

    The engine lays out every Studio diagram at build time with its own deterministic layered layout and writes it into the page as inline SVG followed by a text equivalent. The custom element that holds a diagram adds only pan, zoom and pinch, by changing the SVG's view box. One diagram draws at most the bound spec:consumers.spec-studio.diagrams#design.bound names, and above it the diagram folds, by context and then by layer, as that Spec states.

  • The Studio is built from custom elements, not a framework

    The Studio is built from Web Components, custom elements written without React, Vue, Svelte or another framework.

51. The Studio is built from custom elements, not a framework

spec:decisions.studio-web-components

The Studio is built from custom elements, not a framework

spec:decisions.studio-web-componentsDecision Record · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/decisions/studio-web-components.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding none, verifier binding none, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Let each Studio view work in an HTML page that can load its element script and supply graph data without imposing a framework on that page.
Decision
context
The Studio's views must work inside the Studio and in HTML pages that can load the element script and supply its graph data, such as an exported report, and its assets should stay small and cache well.
decision
The Studio is built from Web Components, custom elements written without React, Vue, Svelte or another framework.
rationale
  • Custom elements avoid a matching framework runtime in every embedding page; the host loads the Studio's element script and supplies the graph data.
  • Element names and attributes are a public embedding contract that is costly to replace; in exchange for framework-independent embedding, the Studio supplies rendering and state handling within its elements.
alternatives
  • Components of React, Vue or Svelte would impose that framework on every page that embeds one of them.
consequences
  • The few elements that need richer state, the harness and the scenario editor, may use a small reactive primitive inside themselves, such as @lit/reactive-element or a signals-style atom, without imposing a framework on the page that embeds them.
  • A host that strips scripts, such as a pull request description, shows a static link to a Studio page, never an element.

52. The build renders every Studio view, and an element only enhances it

spec:decisions.studio-build-renders

The build renders every Studio view, and an element only enhances it

spec:decisions.studio-build-rendersDecision Record · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/decisions/studio-build-renders.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding none, verifier binding none, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Let every Studio view read in full without script, print, and travel inside a Pack export, while its custom element adds only the interaction the view needs.
Decision
context
The custom-elements decision frames an element as a view that renders from graph data its host page supplies. The Studio's pages read in full without script and open from file://, a Pack export carries no script, two builds of one graph write the same bytes, and the page computes no join, claim, fact or floor; the page elements the Studio ships already add behavior to markup the build wrote.
decision
The build renders every Studio view into the page's markup from reader values and the recipe answers its page names, and a custom element adds only the interaction its view needs; a host page that embeds a view carries the markup the build wrote and loads the element script, and supplies no graph data.
rationale
  • A view rendered at build time reads without script, prints, survives the Pack export, and keeps one graph to one set of bytes.
  • An element that holds no graph data cannot compute a join, claim, fact or floor in the browser, which the Studio refuses.
alternatives
  • Elements that render their views from graph data a host supplies, as the custom-elements decision first framed them, show nothing without script and put a second rendering path in the browser.
consequences
  • An element's attributes name its subject and its interaction, never a setting the build did not render, so the original's readiness-pill, depth, highlight and group-by attributes are gone.
  • The custom-elements decision still rules how the elements are written: as custom elements without a framework.
