53. The engine lays out every Studio diagram as static SVG when the page set is built

spec:decisions.studio-diagram-renderer

The engine lays out every Studio diagram as static SVG when the page set is built

spec:decisions.studio-diagram-rendererDecision Record · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/decisions/studio-diagram-renderer.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding none, verifier binding none, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Give the Studio diagrams that a reader with only a link reads without script, that two builds of one graph draw byte for byte, and that need no layout code in the page.
Decision
context
The Studio's pages read in full without script and open from file://, two builds of one graph write the same bytes, and the custom-elements decision admits a framework runtime only through a decision that refines it. The architecture lens, a component's members, a Spec's relations and the code that realizes a Spec all need a drawing. A prototype over the Protocol's own components and the first adopter's, read through sdp q, measured how large those drawings are (reviews/assets/plan46-prototypes/studio-diagrams/).
decision
The engine lays out every Studio diagram at build time with its own deterministic layered layout and writes it into the page as inline SVG followed by a text equivalent. The custom element that holds a diagram adds only pan, zoom and pinch, by changing the SVG's view box. One diagram draws at most the bound spec:consumers.spec-studio.diagrams#design.bound names, and above it the diagram folds, by context and then by layer, as that Spec states.
rationale
  • Inline SVG reads without script, prints, survives the Pack export and opens from file://, so the page carries no layout code and the element stays small.
  • A layout computed from graph values, with no font, clock or random value, draws the same bytes from the same graph, which the Studio's reproducibility rule and --check-clean need.
  • The bound sits between what the two corpora need and what a page reads well: in the prototype the largest real drawing is the Protocol's thirty-five-box member diagram, and a synthetic sixty-two-component drawing spanned about two and a half screen widths unfolded; nothing between forty and sixty-two boxes was measured, and the edge bound is headroom over the thirty-nine edges the largest real diagram draws.
alternatives
  • Mermaid rendered in the page needs its script and a runtime of several hundred kilobytes, lays out differently per browser, and shows nothing without script; the shipped Mermaid projection stays frozen for its own readers.
  • A layout library such as ELK or Dagre run at build time adds a dependency whose version moves the bytes, while the Studio's diagrams need only labelled bands and a grid.
  • Drawing on a canvas from embedded data puts the diagram out of reach of a screen reader, of print and of a reader without script.
consequences
  • The engine owns a small layout module and its tests; the layout's look is judged in review, and its determinism and fold by test.
  • The text equivalent states every box and edge, so a diagram is never the only way to read what it shows.
  • A change to the layout moves the Studio's bytes like any other rendering change, and --check-clean catches one nobody intended.

specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

Every Studio diagram is laid out in the engine when the page set is built, so a page draws it with no script and the same inputs draw the same bytes. The architecture grid, component members and one-hop trace retain their readings; the Spec page's requirement drawing replaces realization, and other pages name their supplied drawing answers. Words carry every reading the picture shows, and its text equivalent states every box and edge.

Intent
outcome
Draw the Studio's diagrams as inline SVG that reads without script, prints, and stays the same bytes for the same graph, with every box and edge also stated in words.
Contract
rule.buildTime line 24 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:24
The build lays out each diagram and writes it into its page as inline SVG; no diagram is laid out in the browser, and a page draws every diagram with no script.

spec:consumers.spec-studio.diagrams.within-bound · enabled

rule.layoutInputs line 25 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:25
A layout reads only the boxes, each with its id, words and supplied grouping, and edges, each with its two ends, exact kind and claim, optional reason and aggregation count, taken from the reader values and recipe answers its page names; it reads no font, file, clock or random value, measures text by character count and writes whole-pixel coordinates. Depth, reach and component resolution belong to those answers, never layout.

spec:consumers.spec-studio.diagrams.within-bound · enabled

rule.sameBytes line 26 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:26
One graph and the same inputs draw byte-identical SVG on every build and every machine.

spec:consumers.spec-studio.diagrams.folds-by-context · enabled, spec:consumers.spec-studio.diagrams.within-bound · enabled

rule.architectureGrid line 27 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:27
The architecture diagram places each component in the column of its recorded context, contexts in code-unit order and then a column for components that state none, and in the band of its layer, in the order edge, application, domain, adapter, infrastructure, then a band for components that state none; a cell holds its components in id order.

spec:consumers.spec-studio.diagrams.within-bound · enabled

rule.aggregatedUses line 28 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:28
An architecture edge joins two components and carries the count of unit uses edges between them, as the component rows of spec:consumers.spec-studio.lenses.architecture#design.componentRows count them: each end of a unit uses edge resolves to its component, directly or through memberOf, and a use within one component draws nothing.

rule.relationBands line 29 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:29
A trace graph draws the Spec in a band of its own, the Specs its declared relations name above it in one band per relation type, in the order refines, dependsOn, constrainedBy, decidedBy, verifies, supersedes, and the Specs whose declared relations name it below in bands of the same order; a Spec related more than one way sits in the band of its first relation, and each relation is its own edge.

no example exercises it

rule.memberBands line 30 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:30
A member diagram draws a component's members in bands by how deep uses among members reaches, a member that uses another sitting above it, and the units and components outside the component that members use in a last band of their own.

rule.wordsBesideStyle line 37 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:37
Every reading a fill, outline or line style marks is also in words: bands and columns carry labels, a planned component reads planned, a folded box reads folded, and an aggregated edge's count is in its text equivalent. A drawing whose edges all have one relation names it once in its legend and draws no edge label; solid uses and dashed plans to use share the use relation, with the planned wording also in the legend. A drawing with several relations keeps its labelled bands and edge labels.

rule.panZoomOnly line 39 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:39
The diagram element adds only pan, zoom and pinch by changing the SVG's view box; it never moves a box or edge. At viewport widths of at least 720 CSS pixels the SVG starts at natural size inside a keyboard-accessible scroll region, with overflow inside the figure. Below that width the responsive contract fits the same drawing to the screen. Reset restores the initial view and scroll position. Without script the drawing, scrolling, links and text equivalent remain usable. Print fits the drawing to paper and exposes its text equivalent.

Design
bound line 42 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:42
40 boxes and 100 edges per diagram, counting every box a drawing holds, folded and planned boxes included, and every edge it draws.

no citation recorded

labelMetrics line 43 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:43
A title or recorded label leads at fourteen pixels, followed by the displayed id at twelve pixels and remaining words such as a component's member count. Title lines hold at most 28 characters and id lines 30, with an eight-pixel character advance. Wrap at spaces or id punctuation, then by code point, and calculate box height from every line.
cellWrap line 44 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:44
Wrap a cell's boxes within the fixed logical width budget instead of a fixed box count; retain context columns with local scrolling when they exceed it. Layout reads no browser or font measurement.
widthBudget line 45 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:45
880 logical pixels for a band or grid, band labels included above their band; 264 per context cell when several contexts share a grid, the full band budget when only one context is shown, and 24 between boxes. Routing gutters may widen the SVG to preserve distinct lanes. A drawing wider than 880 scrolls inside its figure and receives the build-written instruction Scroll horizontally to read the whole drawing.

Reserve boxes and labels as obstacles, route orthogonally with distinct ports and lanes eight pixels apart, and never share a collinear segment or overlap labels. svgMarkup line 49 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:49
the svg carries role="img", a title, aria-describedby naming its text equivalent and a viewBox of its own size; a box is a g with class node and data-id, plus data-planned="true" or data-folded="true" when it is planned or folded, holding a link to the box's target; an edge is a g with class edge, data-from, data-to and data-kind; a band is a g with class band and data-label, a column a g with class lane and data-label, each also drawing its label as text. An edge also carries data-claim and a stable data-edge-key when its label uses a legend key; route and label coordinates are presentation values and mint no graph edge.

a component's box links to its detail on the architecture lens, a planned component's to its component design's Spec page, a context's or layer's folded box to its section on the same page, a Spec's to its page, and a folded relation group's to the Spec page's relations.

a details element closed by default, summary The diagram as text, holding one li per box, <id>: <words>, followed by · folded members: <ids> when folded identities are present, and then one li per edge, <from> <kind> <to>, followed by · <claim> when present, (<n> unit edges) when the edge aggregates more than one, and — <reason> when present.
diagramElement line 52 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.diagrams.sdp.md:52
sdp-diagram with subject, the rooted Spec, Pack, component or context id, or architecture, wraps one figure containing its caption and legend, any build-written scroll instruction, a keyboard-focusable named .diagram-scroll region containing the SVG, its text equivalent and, when offered, its closed Mermaid-source disclosure with labelled read-only textarea and sdp-copy. Caption, legend and source stay outside the scroll region. On upgrade it adds Zoom in, Zoom out and Reset buttons and handles drag, a wheel with Control or Command held, and pinch; it adds no layout or copy behavior.

a diagram's text equivalent has the id diagram.<subject>.text and its arrow has the id diagram.<subject>.arrow. Design view

Requirement drawing

  • Declared verifying examples: no declared verifying example.

Decisions

  • The engine lays out every Studio diagram as static SVG when the page set is built

    The engine lays out every Studio diagram at build time with its own deterministic layered layout and writes it into the page as inline SVG followed by a text equivalent. The custom element that holds a diagram adds only pan, zoom and pinch, by changing the SVG's view box. One diagram draws at most the bound spec:consumers.spec-studio.diagrams#design.bound names, and above it the diagram folds, by context and then by layer, as that Spec states.

A few custom elements filter, search, open and copy on a rendered page

specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The build renders every page whole, so these elements add behavior to markup that is already there rather than rendering views of their own. A browser refuses a module script on a page opened through file://, so they ship as one classic script.

Intent
outcome
Give the Studio's pages their few interactions through custom elements that enhance markup the build wrote, so a page with its script filters, searches and copies, and every page but the search page still reads in full without it.
Contract
rule.oneScript line 21 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md:21
The elements ship in one classic script, assets/studio.js, with no module syntax and nothing loaded at run time; the build bundles it from the package's source, with the concept matcher.

no example exercises it

rule.enhanceOnly line 22 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md:22
Each element enhances markup the build wrote and renders no graph value of its own, except that the search results element renders values from the search index its page embeds.

no example exercises it

rule.noRequest line 23 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md:23
No element requests anything on a page opened through file://; the stamp element requests stamp.json only over http or https.

no example exercises it

rule.nativeControls line 24 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md:24

no example exercises it

rule.liveCounts line 25 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md:25

no example exercises it

Design
search line 28 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md:28
sdp-search with page-root, the relative path from its page to the page-set root: wraps the search field's form and, on submit, opens <page-root>search.html#q=<term> with the term percent-encoded.

no citation recorded

searchResults line 29 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md:29
sdp-search-results: on the search page, reads the index from the sdp-data element, matches the fragment's term and each term the person types, writes the results spec:consumers.spec-studio.search designs, and keeps the term in the fragment.

no citation recorded

filter line 30 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md:30
sdp-filter: wraps a hidden form of labelled select elements, each with data-filter="<name>" and an any option, and the rows marked data-row. On upgrade it shows the form, hides each row whose data-<name> differs from a chosen value, and writes <shown> of <total> shown in its output element; a row whose attribute holds several space-separated values, such as its Packs, matches when one of them equals the choice.

no citation recorded

expander line 31 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md:31
sdp-expander: adds Open all and Close all buttons for the details elements inside it, and on load and on each fragment change opens every details that holds the fragment's target and scrolls the target into view.

no citation recorded

copy line 32 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md:32
sdp-copy with text, or with for naming a text area on its page: a Copy button whose accessible name includes the text or the text area's label; it copies that text and says Copied, and where the clipboard is unavailable it selects the text so the person can copy it.

no citation recorded

stamp line 33 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.page-elements.sdp.md:33

59. The Studio reads on a phone as on a desktop

spec:consumers.spec-studio.responsive

The Studio reads on a phone as on a desktop

spec:consumers.spec-studio.responsiveUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: 3 design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/spec-studio.responsive.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The curated graph's edges carry no confidence, and the impact graph's inferred imports stay outside it, so a diagram never drops an edge for a low score; a trace graph draws one hop at every width, and a narrow screen scales the drawing rather than cutting it.

Intent
actor
A person reviewing a design on a phone, including a pull request reviewer who holds only a link.
outcome
Let a design be reviewed on a phone through the same pages a desktop shows.
Behavior
rule line 19 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.responsive.sdp.md:19
Every page of the Studio is responsive, so the same pages serve a desktop and a phone.

1 unkeyed rule.

Example space

Given a Studio page whose layout holds {wideColumns:number} columns
When the page is shown {width:number} pixels wide
Then the layout holds {columns:number} columns
UI
singleColumn line 22 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.responsive.sdp.md:22
every layout collapses to one column below 720 CSS pixels of viewport width; at 390 CSS pixels no page exceeds the viewport. The top navigation and stamp line wrap, and a table wider than its column scrolls inside its own container, including maturity maps, run results and coverage tables; queue rows wrap within their column.
pinchZoom line 23 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.responsive.sdp.md:23
on a touch device, every diagram zooms with a pinch, which the diagram element adds.
narrowDiagram line 24 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.responsive.sdp.md:24
below the same width a diagram opens scaled to the screen's width, with its zoom controls above it and its text equivalent below it, and draws the same boxes and edges a desktop draws.

specs/consumers/spec-studio.export.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

A design is sent and archived as well as browsed: attached to a message, handed to someone outside the repository, printed for a review meeting. Every build writes each Pack as one self-contained HTML file inside the page set, so a reader with only a link downloads it from the Pack page, and the file opens anywhere with nothing beside it. Every page also prints as a document.

Intent
outcome
Let a person take a Pack's whole design away as one file that opens anywhere, and print any page as a readable document.
Behavior

62. A Studio build is stamped and shared from a static host

spec:consumers.spec-studio.sharing

A Studio build is stamped and shared from a static host

spec:consumers.spec-studio.sharingUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:self-hosting-v1, pack:spec-studio-v1

Design: 9 design entries · 3 pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/spec-studio.sharing.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

A page set is a function of the graph and its named inputs, so it carries no commit or time. A reviewer opening a preview still needs to know which commit and which engine built it, so a publishing step that runs after the build writes one stamp file at the page set's root, and the shell shows it where the set is served over http or https. The same stamp may name where the repository's source is served, so a recorded file and line become a link in a preview and stay text everywhere else. A reusable workflow does the build, the stamp and the upload for every pull request, and deploys a preview only where the repository has chosen a host. Checks and previews use GitHub's default pull-request merge checkout, so the gate proves the merge result and the run evidence, page set and stamp name that same commit.

A stakeholder opens the link, navigates the Studio and composes intent, and the pull request's author hands that intent to an agent that edits the source.

Intent
outcome
Let a stakeholder open the Studio of a pull request from a link, and let its author know which graph and which build the stakeholder read.
Behavior
rule line 25 · specs/consumers/spec-studio.sharing.sdp.md:25
A build is shared by uploading its page set to a static host, such as S3, Vercel or GitHub Pages.

The Studio's build writes no stamp, so every page and data file it writes stays a function of the graph and its named inputs; the stamp is written apart, after the build.

Intent
outcome
Execute the stamp step apart from the build: it touches no page, and no stamp outlives its build.
assumptions
  • The world writes a root with one Pack of two member Specs, runs the studio command, keeps the bytes of every page file, runs the stamp command, reads stamp.json and compares the page files with the kept bytes, then runs the studio command again and checks whether stamp.json exists.

specs/consumers/studio-on-ramp.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The Studio's work reaches an agent in three forms: a person or an agent holding only a link, a coding agent that publishes pages or receives intent a person composed in them, and a developer who sets up previews in CI. Each needs steps that most graph questions never use, so the Studio has its own skill and the reading skill points to it.

Intent
outcome
Give an agent a shipped on-ramp that publishes and shares the Spec Studio, reads it by task from a repository or a link, and turns intent composed in it into checked carrier edits.
Behavior

The Studio is taught in its own shipped skill, beside the reading, authoring and session skills, and the reading skill points to it.
